title: Semiotic Complexity and Its Epistemological Implications for Modeling Culture
abstract: arXiv:2508.00095v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Greater theorizing of methods in the computational humanities is needed for epistemological and interpretive clarity, and therefore the maturation of the field. In this paper, we frame such modeling work as engaging in translation work from a cultural, linguistic domain into a computational, mathematical domain, and back again. Translators benefit from articulating the theory of their translation process, and so do computational humanists in their work -- to ensure internal consistency, avoid subtle yet consequential translation errors, and facilitate interpretive transparency. Our contribution in this paper is to lay out a particularly consequential dimension of the lack of theorizing and the sorts of translation errors that emerge in our modeling practices as a result. translated_title: 符号学复杂性及其对文化建模的认识论意涵
translated_abstract: 计算人文学科需要对方法进行更深入的理论化，以获得认识论与阐释层面的清晰性，进而推动该领域的成熟。在本文中，我们将此类建模工作框定为一种翻译活动：即从文化的、语言学的领域转换到计算的、数学的领域，再转换回来。译者会因清晰阐明其翻译过程的理论而受益，计算人文学者在工作中同样如此——以确保内部一致性、避免微妙却影响重大的翻译错误，并促进阐释的透明性。本文的贡献在于揭示了理论化缺失中一个尤为关键的维度，以及由此在我们的建模实践中产生的各类翻译错误。沿着这一思路，我们引入了“符号学复杂性”这一概念，即某一文本的含义在不同阐释视角之间可能发生变化的程度，并论证了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出“符号学复杂性”概念——即文本含义在不同阐释视角下的变化程度——将计算人文的建模视为从文化语言领域到计算数学领域的翻译过程，并论证缺乏翻译理论化会导致微妙而影响深远的建模错误。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "semiotic complexity"—the degree to which a text's meaning may vary across interpretive lenses—framing computational humanities modeling as translation between cultural-linguistic and computational-mathematical domains, and showing how the lack of theorizing about translation leads to subtle yet consequential modeling errors.
